UC8 breaks the AC8 sequence. It runs COB on 31 January and the repayment first, then runs COB on 28, 29 and 30 January. The business date goes backwards, so “accruals continue for the remaining days in January after the first repayment” cannot be verified. The “number invented” flag is correct, because the dates and the year 2027 are not in the AC. Only the UC8 dates contradict the AC, so I counted that defect once under D_ORDER, not D_NUM.

State sequence is not business-valid. UC8 moves COB from 31 January back to 28, 29 and 30 January, which is impossible for a business date. The expected accruals for those days cannot follow from that sequence.

Resume dates do not match the current business date (AC4, AC11). AC4 allows resume only when the resume start date equals the current business date. Every scenario sets the business date to 01 January 2027 and never changes it, yet successful resumes use 01 February, 20 January and 25 January. In UC5, the rejection at 15 January cannot be attributed to “same as pause start”, because today is still 01 January. This invented-number flag is confirmed, since these dates directly contradict AC4.

Resume happens before the pause is active. The pause starts on 15 January, but the business date stays at 01 January and is never advanced before the resume. So a pause that has not started yet is resumed and checked as if it were active (like a repayment before disbursement).
